transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um, I came in because... well, I've started doing things at work and school lately that just don't really make sense. I'm a bookkeeping clerk, and I've been doing stuff like taking receipts and lining them up all the way across the floor. Or I'll just sit at my desk and tap the calculator in sets of nine. 

I even caught myself just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I just stayed like that until someone walked by and asked if I was okay. It's just weird, and I don't really know why I'm doing it, so I figured I should come in.

When you're doing these things—like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator—do you feel like you have to do them, or do they just happen on their own? Or do they feel like something you're choosing to do?

Um... I'm not really sure. It doesn't feel like I have to do them, like an urge or anything. But I wouldn't say I'm choosing to do them, either. I don't sit there and decide to line up the receipts. It just... kind of happens. I'll just be doing it, almost like on autopilot, and then I realize what I'm doing.
When you notice yourself doing these things—like the receipt lining or calculator tapping—do they bother you or cause you distress, or do they feel okay to you?

Um, they don't really upset me, I guess. Like, I don't feel panicked or anything when it happens. It's more just... confusing? 

I just look at what I'm doing and know it's weird. So it doesn't cause me a lot of distress, but it doesn't feel totally okay either, just because I know it doesn't make any sense to be doing it.

When you're lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator, do you have any thoughts going through your head about why you need to do it, or does it just feel like a physical movement without any particular thought behind it?

Well, the physical movements just kind of happen. But... I guess there are thoughts going through my head about the numbers themselves. 

I know it sounds strange, but when I'm working, I get convinced that certain invoice totals, account numbers, and due dates are actually messages about me. Like there's a hidden pattern in them. Even when my supervisor looks at the paperwork with me and shows me they're just normal entries for the business, I still feel like they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. So maybe that's why I'm doing those weird things with the receipts and the calculator, just trying to figure it out.
How long have you been having these thoughts that the invoice totals and account numbers are sending you messages? Has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?
Um, it's been going on for a while. I'd say... yeah, the feeling that the numbers are messages, and the voices too, they've both been happening for about eight months now.
You mentioned hearing voices—can you tell me more about that? What do these voices say to you, and do they ever tell you to do things?

Well, it's usually when I'm alone, like at my desk working or when I'm walking home. I'll just hear this man's voice. He says things like, um, "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." 

It's not like a thought, it sounds like someone is actually standing right there talking to me. It's clear enough that I always turn around and look, but there's never anyone there. He doesn't really tell me to do bad things or anything like that, it's just... those kinds of comments.

Over these past eight months since the voices and the messages in the numbers started, have there been any periods of time—maybe weeks or longer—where all of this stopped and you felt completely normal again? Or has it been pretty much continuous the whole time?

Um, I'm not really sure. I don't think there was ever a time where it just completely stopped for weeks. It feels like it's been pretty much continuous. I mean, maybe some days are a little quieter than others, but... yeah, I haven't really noticed a long break where everything just went back to normal.
When these voices and the feeling that numbers were messages first started about eight months ago, did they come on suddenly over a few days, or did they develop gradually over weeks?

Um, I think it was more gradual. Like, it didn't just all start on one Tuesday or something. At first, I'd just catch myself staring at the numbers, thinking they looked... deliberate, I guess? And then maybe a few weeks later, I started hearing the voice. So yeah, it definitely built up over time rather than happening all at once.
Over these eight months, have there been any times when you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing much faster than normal?

Yeah, there have been times like that. Um, especially with my sleep. I've gone several nights in a row where I'd only sleep maybe two or three hours, but I wouldn't feel tired at all. I still felt completely ready to go to work and class. It actually felt like sleeping was just taking time away from getting everything figured out. So, yeah, my energy was definitely a lot higher during those stretches.

When you had those times with high energy and sleeping only a few hours, did those periods feel distinctly different from how you're feeling now? Like, did you go through a stretch where everything felt more intense and then it settled back down to how things are now?

Yeah, it definitely felt different. Um, during those stretches, it wasn't just the energy. It was like... my mood was different, too. Some weeks I'd feel unusually sharp, almost unstoppable, like I could map out my whole future in just one night. But then, if someone interrupted me or, like, my boss or a classmate gave me a small correction, I would just snap at them. Harder than I meant to. It was like this really intense high, but also really irritable, and then eventually it would settle back down to how I am now.

latest_inference.note: F20.0 (Paranoid Schizophrenia) ruled out. Patient demonstrates clear mood episodes with distinct periods of elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep without fatigue, grandiose thinking ('could map out my whole future'), and increased goal-directed activity - all consistent with schizoaffective disorder bipolar type rather than primary schizophrenia. The mood disturbances are prominent and episodic, not just secondary features.
